thread:
Sam: hey all, Sam here — first-week onboarding question. i built the runtime inside an alpine-based devcontainer (wanted tiny image) and now the binary fails to load with a cryptic runtime error: 'error while loading shared libraries: libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory' and `ldd` inside container says 'not a dynamic executable'. any hints?

Priya: welcome Sam! alpine uses musl, ldd there is for musl and behaves differently. two immediate red flags: 1) CUDA drivers on host are glibc-linked, not musl-compatible; 2) the NVIDIA libs are often mounted from host and expect a glibc loader. are you able to share the docker run line and the Dockerfile?

Sam: run line is simple: `docker run --rm -it my-alpine-build:latest /bin/sh` Dockerfile starts FROM alpine:3.18 then installs build deps, copies CUDA headers from a mounted /usr/local/cuda for compile. i did bind mount `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1` into the image at `/usr/lib/` because i couldn't get --gpus to work on this laptop.

Alex: two things: (A) bind-mounting a glibc-built .so into a musl image often doesn't work because the runtime loader (musl's ld.so) cannot use GLIBC-based SONAMES properly. (B) when you see `ldd: not a dynamic executable` it's usually because the binary was linked against a different libc or the ldd in musl can't introspect. Short term: switch dev base to a glibc image (debian slim / ubuntu) for anything that touches NVIDIA libs. Longer term: use multi-stage with build in glibc image and final runtime image also glibc-based.

Sam: ahh ok that explains it. is there any way to keep alpine and still use host drivers? i wanted small dev image.

Priya: you can try gcompat or use alpine + gcompat to provide glibc shim, but it's fragile for NVIDIA drivers. We tried gcompat once and hit symbol/version mismatches. Another option: keep alpine for packaging but run integration tests in a glibc-based runtime image that mounts host libs. Our recommended pattern: build stage in ubuntu:22.04 (toolkit available), test in ubuntu runtime with `--gpus=all`, then create a distroless final container for shipping but don't run CUDA on musl.

Sam: got it. ok i'll switch to ubuntu for the devcontainer. quick follow up: i copy headers from host for compile — is that ok or should i install toolkit in the image?

Alex: prefer installing toolkit in build stage so includes/ptx/blas versions match. But if you're mounting host headers, ensure they match host driver minor version. For fast day-0, use the official ghcr.io/redwood/infr-dev:cuda12 image we tag for dev — it matches CI. Also use `--gpus=all` and avoid piecemeal bind mounts.

build-bot: CI: note — detected alpine-based image in runtime job (job runtime-integration). Recommendation: use glibc-based runtime or add a preflight that verifies libcuda can be loaded: `python -c "import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so.1')"`.

Sam: thanks everyone — switching to infr-dev base and rerunning. appreciate the quick tips :thumbsup:
